comments.author: quangdang46
comments.text: Audit findings: PLAN.md is the canonical planning and milestone source for Beads translation because it contains the fullest end-to-end product, architecture, module, and milestone structure. AGENTS.md is canonical for workflow/coordination rules, including Beads, bv, session discipline, and multi-agent norms. README.md is product-facing and useful for positioning, but it is currently aspirational and not authoritative for exact implemented command surface because it documents commands like 'file', 'fn', and 'tree' while the current CLI exposes 'deps', 'symbols', 'calls', 'callers', and 'impact'. POC.md is supplemental/historical validation material for the optional Node.js proof of concept and informs extraction/query semantics, but it is not the execution source of truth. PLAN-claude.md and plan-codex.md were referenced in the bead description but do not exist in the repository at present, so they should not be treated as active sources until added. Translation rule: use PLAN.md for milestone/epic/task decomposition, use AGENTS.md for workflow constraints, use README.md only to reconcile user-facing claims, and use POC.md only when deciding whether to pursue/defer/retire the POC track.

title: Define Beads taxonomy, naming, and comment conventions
description: Define issue type usage, priority usage, labeling, title style, and the self-documenting metadata template that will be used across the Beads graph.
design: Intent: make the graph consistent and machine/human-scannable. Include title patterns, when to split subtasks, how to encode non-goals, and how to reference source docs/sections in issue metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy and naming rules are explicit. Comment/description/design/acceptance/notes templates are reusable. Priority choices are justified and consistently applicable across milestones.
notes: Future self note: the quality of the issue graph depends more on consistent conventions than on having a large number of issues.
close_reason: Completed: taxonomy, naming, labeling, and comment conventions defined

comments.author: quangdang46
comments.text: Proposed Beads conventions for this repository: 1) Issue types: use 'epic' for milestone-level containers or multi-track deliverables; use 'task' for execution-sized units that a single focused session or agent can complete or advance meaningfully. Avoid creating subtasks so small that they become diary entries rather than planning artifacts. 2) Priority scale: P1 = foundational blockers, top-level coordination work, or tasks that unlock major downstream tracks; P2 = important milestone work and documentation/behavior alignment that materially reduces risk; P3 = useful follow-on capabilities, polish, or later-stage workflow features; P4 = backlog or speculative extensions. Choose priority by unblock value and roadmap order, not by personal interest. 3) Title style: use imperative, outcome-oriented titles that start with a strong verb such as Add, Implement, Persist, Create, Document, Decide, Align, Encode, Validate, or Stabilize. Titles should describe the user-visible or graph-visible outcome, not the step-by-step implementation diary. 4) Labels: assign 2-4 labels max, typically one domain label (e.g. file-graph, symbols, impact), one implementation surface label (cli, sqlite, tests, docs, agents), and when helpful one planning/governance label. Prefer reuse of existing labels over inventing near-duplicates. 5) Description/design/acceptance/notes template: Description explains why the task exists and its boundary. Design states objective, scope, and non-goals. Acceptance criteria are concrete and observable. Notes capture future-self cautions, dependency intent, or trust boundaries. 6) Dependency rules: encode true prerequisites only. Parent-child links organize hierarchy; blocks links represent real execution order. Prefer explicit blockers where one task materially unlocks another. 7) Source citation rule: when a task is derived from PLAN.md or another canonical doc, mention the relevant concept or section in the description/design rather than embedding long quotations. 8) Comment conventions: use comments to record decisions, classification outcomes, scope clarifications, and execution guidance that should survive beyond a single session. Comments should be concise, durable, and decision-oriented rather than stream-of-consciousness status logs. 9) Granularity rule: a task deserves its own issue when it has distinct acceptance criteria, can be meaningfully blocked/unblocked, or can be assigned independently; otherwise keep the detail inside the parent issue comment or design text. 10) Beads graph quality principle: favor a smaller, dependency-accurate graph with rich metadata over a large noisy graph with ambiguous titles or weak acceptance criteria.

acceptance_criteria: All major milestones have child tasks. Granularity is sufficient for parallel work and explicit blockers. Issue metadata is rich enough to stand alone.
notes: Future self note: if a task title starts looking like an implementation diary entry, it is probably too small to deserve its own issue.

comments.author: quangdang46
comments.text: Milestone decomposition audit: the execution graph already contained milestone epics for Phase 0, Milestones 0-10, and docs/governance work, but later roadmap milestones were under-decomposed relative to PLAN.md sections 17.11-17.14. To satisfy this bead's acceptance criteria and the conventions established in scope-2d1.11, I verified existing milestone coverage against PLAN.md milestone headings and filled the most obvious granularity gaps in late-stage roadmap work. Added explicit child tasks for Milestone 11 (utility queries; doctor/benchmark foundations; multi-language integration validation), Milestone 12 (cochange analysis; simulate extract workflow; fixtures/golden validation), Milestone 13 (entry-point reachability; capability audit; split/mirror guidance), and Milestone 14 (report/gate flows; serve/web UI; query language/REPL). Existing earlier milestones already had at least one or more executable child tasks and did not require immediate structural repair during this pass. Remaining work belongs to scope-2d1.13: verify blocker relationships and parallel tracks now that milestone/task coverage is more complete.

title: Encode dependency graph and parallel execution tracks
description: Add blocker relationships so the Beads graph reflects the real execution order while preserving parallel tracks where tasks are independent.
design: Intent: make br ready meaningful. Focus on hard prerequisites only, with enough independence to allow scaffolding, validation, docs, and fixtures to move in parallel. Non-goals: over-constraining the graph.
acceptance_criteria: Critical dependency chains are represented. There are no obvious accidental cycles. Parallelizable work remains available once prerequisite roots are satisfied.
notes: Future self note: an empty br ready list usually means the graph is over-constrained, not that the project has no work.
close_reason: Completed: dependency graph audited, no cycles found, and parallel tracks remain sensible

comments.author: quangdang46
comments.text: Dependency/parallelism audit findings: reviewed representative dependency chains with br dep tree, br dep list, br blocked, br ready, and bv --robot-triage. The graph has no dependency cycles. Ready work remains concentrated on foundation, planning, docs, and the optional POC path rather than on late-stage roadmap items, which means the graph is not accidentally surfacing advanced milestones ahead of prerequisites. Existing blocker chains already encode the main execution order from foundation -> file graph -> symbols -> call graph -> impact -> context/incremental -> architecture/surface/integration -> utilities/simulation/topology/reporting. Newly added late-stage tasks for Milestones 11-14 currently inherit their effective sequencing through their parent epics, and they are not appearing as ready work, so additional direct blocker edges are not necessary in this pass. Avoiding extra direct blockers preserves parallelism and reduces over-constraint, which aligns with this bead's goal. Result: dependency graph is coherent enough to hand off to graph-quality verification in scope-2d1.14.

title: Verify Beads graph quality with br and bv outputs
description: Validate that the created graph behaves correctly under Beads and bv triage tools, including ready work, blockers, and recommendation ordering.
design: Intent: test the execution substrate itself. Use br list/show/ready and bv --robot-triage/--robot-plan/--robot-suggest to verify structure, not just issue existence.
acceptance_criteria: Triage output is sensible. Foundation/planning/fixture work appears before late-stage features. Sample issues are self-contained and blocker relationships are coherent.
notes: Future self note: this task is the guardrail against a pretty-but-useless issue graph.
close_reason: Completed: br and bv outputs confirm the graph is coherent and usable

comments.author: quangdang46
comments.text: Graph-quality verification results: br ready still prioritizes foundation, planning, docs, and the optional POC path ahead of later roadmap capabilities; bv --robot-triage continues to surface foundation/file-graph work as the most important technical path; bv --robot-plan shows multiple parallel tracks rather than an over-constrained serial chain; br blocked and br dep tree confirm coherent blocker structure; br dep cycles reports no dependency cycles. Sample late-stage tasks (for Milestones 11-14) remain non-ready through their epic prerequisites, while foundation tasks such as scope-2d1.2.3, scope-2d1.2.4, and scope-2d1.2.5 remain ready. bv --robot-suggest produced optional label and possible dependency suggestions, but nothing indicated a structural failure severe enough to block use of the graph. Conclusion: the Beads execution graph is useful, dependency-aware, and triage-sensible for continued work.

Scope: shortest-path explanation (`scope why`), minimum context selection (`scope context`), token-budget context packs (`scope pack`), and their output contracts. References: PLAN.md goals, CLI contract, JSON contract, and Milestone 5. Non-goals: speculative UI work or broad later analytics not needed for these workflows.
acceptance_criteria: scope why, scope context, and scope pack are each represented by concrete executable child tasks. Acceptance criteria for each are tied to command behavior, output shape, and fixture coverage.
notes: Dependency notes: this milestone builds on the core graph and impact machinery, but it is distinct from incremental indexing and should remain visible as a first-class user-facing milestone.

notes: Expected first areas: query/graph traversal logic, output contract, and fixture cases with multiple plausible paths.

acceptance_criteria: scope context identifies targets, ranks must-read/should-read files, and explains inclusion/exclusion decisions in stable output. Results are validated with representative fixtures and command examples.
notes: Expected first areas: query scoring layer, output model, and task-oriented fixtures based on rename/change scenarios.

acceptance_criteria: scope pack respects a provided budget, emits stable pack structure, and preserves the most relevant public surface / caller / callee / impact information for supported scenarios. Validation includes task-based fixtures and output checks.
notes: Expected first areas: context scoring reuse, token estimation/budget enforcement, and pack-format contract design.

comments.author: quangdang46
comments.text: Classification decision: PLAN.md is the canonical planning and execution document for this repository. It is the authoritative source for milestone structure, module responsibilities, roadmap ordering, and issue-graph decomposition. AGENTS.md is canonical for workflow protocol and execution discipline: Beads usage, bv usage, coordination norms, session completion checklist, commit discipline, and other agent-operating rules. README.md is supplemental and product-facing: it should explain the vision and user-facing contract, but it must be reconciled against the implemented CLI and current roadmap rather than treated as the source of truth. POC.md is supplemental/historical: it captures an optional Node.js proof-of-concept path and useful validation ideas, but it is not the main implementation plan. Missing docs note: PLAN-claude.md and plan-codex.md are not present in the repo, so current classification should explicitly mark them as nonexistent/legacy references rather than active planning sources. Future-update rule: put planning and decomposition changes in PLAN.md, workflow/process changes in AGENTS.md, and user-facing capability/usage updates in README.md once they match implementation status.

description: Make sure the README reflects what exists, what is planned, and what remains non-goal or future work so expectations stay honest.

acceptance_criteria: README statements align with actual project maturity and roadmap intent. Overclaims around support, certainty, or completion are removed or clarified.
notes: Future self note: honest README language reduces pressure to promise magic later.
